card.summary: H.R. 5089, the Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2025, updates, expands, and reauthorizes various programs within the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and related federal agencies focused on weather forecasting, research, monitoring, and data collection. The bill establishes new programs and initiatives targeting specific phenomena such as atmospheric rivers, coastal flooding, storm surges, tornadoes, hurricanes, and harmful algal blooms, while also emphasizing commercial weather data acquisition, supercomputing resources, and improved public risk communication.

summary: The National Landslide Preparedness Act Reauthorization Act of 2025 reauthorizes and updates federal programs related to landslide hazards, water observation, and data monitoring. It extends funding authorities, incorporates considerations for atmospheric rivers and extreme precipitation events, establishes regional partnerships and new water observation systems, and expands coordination to include Indian tribes, tribal organizations, and Native Hawaiian organizations.

affected_groups.effect: Must implement new assessment requirements, establish regional partnerships, manage the Next Generation Water Observing System, and handle expanded monitoring and grant responsibilities.
Gains explicit inclusion and consultation rights in landslide preparedness, hazard mitigation, emergency response, and water resource monitoring programs.
affected_groups.group: Indian tribes, Tribal organizations, and Native Hawaiian organizations

affected_groups.effect: Eligible for expanded grant programs, early warning system deployments, and improved real-time risk management tools during landslide and flooding events.
affected_groups.group: State and local governments and emergency managers

key_provisions: Reauthorizes the National Landslide Preparedness Act through fiscal year 2030, increasing authorized funding to $35 million annually and earmarking at least $10 million for early warning systems.
Requires the Secretary of the Interior, in consultation with the Secretary of Commerce, to assess risks that atmospheric river and extreme precipitation events pose to landslide safety.
Establishes a Next Generation Water Observing System within the United States Geological Survey to provide real-time data on water quantity and quality across initial priority basins.
Extends the 3D Elevation Program authorization through fiscal year 2034 and adds a 3D Hydrography Program Working Group.

Expands tribal and indigenous participation by explicitly including Indian tribes, tribal organizations, and Native Hawaiian organizations in grant programs, emergency responses, and advisory committees.
Increases authorization levels for national groundwater monitoring programs to $30 million for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2033.
missing_information: Total mandatory spending figures, as all funding is subject to future appropriations acts.

It extends funding authorities, incorporates considerations for atmospheric rivers and extreme precipitation events, establishes regional partnerships and new water observation systems, and expands coordination to include Indian tribes, tribal organizations, and Native Hawaiian organizations.
summary_detail.significance: The bill moderately modifies federal natural hazard and water resource monitoring frameworks by expanding programs through the 2030s, integrating weather extremes like atmospheric rivers into landslide planning, and funding new real-time observation systems.
